title: Owner labels in the open points name individuals, not roles
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3
section: Section 8 Open points, column Owner; sections 8 and 9 in version 4
description: Six open-point rows give the owner as an individual label rather than a role: DL03, DL04, DL05, DL06, DL07 and DL37. The run forbids person names in any output, so each of those cells now carries the Template and Rules R9 placeholder, with the organisation or role the same row already stated kept after it. The role each label holds is not stated in the source.
evidence: Section 8 column Owner: DL03 one label plus 'with the architecture team'; DL04 one label; DL05 one label; DL06 two labels; DL07 one label; DL37 one label. DL43 already gives a role, 'ACE team lead', and is unchanged. Section 9 Approval states five roles: SCB CTO, SCB IT architecture, ACE team lead, TechX delivery lead, Henka solution architect.
proposed: Confirm the role that owns each of the six open points and record the role, not the individual, in section 8 and in every document that quotes these rows.

title: Version 4 carries the version 3 approval statuses and no approval of the 19-service decision
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v4
section: Section 1 decisions table, column Status; section 9 Approval
description: Version 3 recorded Agreed for the single-service decisions DT07, DT08, DT09 and DT02. The records that replace them, ADR-013, ADR-014, ADR-016 and ADR-017, are Proposed at 22 November 2026, and no approval of version 4 is recorded in any source. The four replaced rows therefore carry Proposed, the unchanged rows keep the version 3 status, section 9 keeps the version 3 statuses word for word, and the document is issued as Draft.
evidence: Version 3 section 1: DT07, DT08, DT09 and DT02 read Agreed; DL07 reads Proposed. Architecture Decision Records v4 index: ADR-013 to ADR-023 all read Proposed, 22 November 2026. Version 3 section 9: SCB CTO and SCB IT architecture To approve; ACE team lead, TechX delivery lead and Henka solution architect Agreed.
proposed: Record the approval of version 4 by SCB CTO and SCB IT architecture, and decide whether the replacing ADRs of 22 November 2026 are accepted with it, so that the status column and section 9 can carry an approved state.

title: The option 3 cells of the workflow comparison are written as not-now and no source restates them
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 3.1 Options compared, column 3 and the verdict row
description: Version 3 recorded option 3, programmatic cases with Temporal for the automation tasks, as 'Not now; can be added for a task under a separate decision', and shaped every option 3 cell for short tasks only. ADR-011 and ADR-016 now put the case lifecycle on Temporal, so the cells are rewritten for a case that is rows plus a durable timer and a child workflow per stage. No source states the rewritten cells.
evidence: Version 3 section 3.1 verdict row reads 'Not now; can be added for a task under a separate decision' for option 3, and its long-wait cell reads 'Cases as rows; Temporal only for short tasks'. Architecture v5 slide 12 gives Temporal in five layers; slide 14 gives CaseWorkflow parent with a child workflow per stage; Architecture Decision Records v4 ADR-016 gives Continue-As-New and one task queue per service; slide 44 moves JOB-05 to durable timers.
proposed: Confirm the rewritten option 3 cells: case state as rows, waits as durable timers, a child workflow per stage, Continue-As-New for a stage that changes, and reporting kept in SQL.

title: Statements about one repository, no extra runtime, Quartz and Spring Batch are not restated for 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 states that the bank runs no extra runtime, that squads release from one repository, that Quartz runs the schedules and Spring Batch the automated chains, and that release is one train with collection. With 19 services, a shared Temporal cluster and one schema per service those statements no longer describe the build. This version restates them from Architecture v5 and the accepted records; no source restates the sentences themselves.
evidence: Version 3 section 3.2 bullet 'The bank runs no extra runtime, and case reporting stays in SQL'; section 3.4 bullets on Quartz and Spring Batch; section 6 'Two TechX squads and the collection squad release from one repository'; section 7 row Release 'One release train with collection'. Architecture v5 slide 12 (one shared Temporal cluster in five layers) and slide 44 (Schedules in the owning service, no shared Quartz tables); ADR-016, ADR-021.
proposed: Confirm the restated sentences: one shared Temporal cluster reused by every workbench, a Schedule in the owning service, one repository and one pipeline per service, and one release train shared with collection with a flag per service.

title: The number of squads that release the 19 services is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 6 How squads merge and release
description: Version 3 names two TechX squads and the collection squad against one repository. Architecture v5 says the 19 services arrive in waves and that one service template keeps the cost per service low, but no source states how many squads, or which team type, releases the 19 services. The sentence keeps the version 3 count, and the assumption records that the count is unchanged.
evidence: Version 3 section 6 'Two TechX squads and the collection squad release from one repository'. Architecture v5 slide 45 'Isn't 19 too many for a team of nine?' answers with waves and one template and names no squad count per service. Template and Rules R5.3 gives owner team types only, as a suggestion.
proposed: State the squad that owns each service in Waves 1 to 4, and whether the two TechX squads and the ACE team cover all 19 services, so that section 6 names the releasing teams by role.

title: Table counts per schema are not stated in any source
source: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Section 5.1 Schema and login per service
description: Version 3 gives the Workbench total of 92 tables, and the Ownership Map fixes the owner of every table, operation, event, job and workflow, but no document states how many of the 92 tables each rwb_* schema holds. The table of 19 schemas therefore carries the owner of each schema and what it owns, and no table count per schema.
evidence: Version 3 section 5 gives 92 tables, 30 views and 1,366 dictionary fields, and no per-schema split. Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows 2 to 94 give one owner code per table; the Read me sheet states no per-service count.
proposed: Publish the table count per rwb_* schema from the Ownership Map, so that section 5.1 can state the count against each service and the Physical Schema folder can be checked against the 92-table total.
